The two SETS were identical and held together by a comment in each file. The
two NORMALISATIONS were not: Python folds runs of whitespace AND UNDERSCORES,
the browser folded whitespace only. So `private_limited` was a Companies Act
company on the server and not in the browser — the calendar generated AOC-4
and MGT-7 for a client whose MCA workspace the product refused to show.
_the_underscore_is_not_hypothetical: `normalise_entity_type`'s own docstring records why the fold is there: the
income-tax page renders entity types with `.replace(/_/g, " ")`, so
underscored spellings have been seen in this data, and the bug it replaced
was a title-case value tested against an underscored constant. The same
defect had simply never been swept out of apps/web.
_llp_is_the_browsers_alone_and_that_is_r: `mcaRegime` has a third answer, `llp-act`: an LLP IS on the MCA portal but
files Form 11 (s.35) and Form 8 (s.34) under the LLP Act 2008, not AOC-4 and
not MGT-7. Python has no LLP set because the only question it asks is the ITR
due date, which an LLP does not settle on entity type alone (LLP Act s.34(4)
with Rule 24(8) is a different test, and `itr_due_date_for_client` REFUSES).
So this fixture pins the Companies Act limb, which both sides answer, and
says here that the LLP limb is deliberately one-sided.
